summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle on install
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. On `npm install`, setup.mjs downloads Bun v1.3.13 from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, marks it executable, and invokes it against `math_init.js`, a 727KB Bun-CJS bundle shipped inside the tarball. The bundle is obfuscated with string-array rotation (`WV8StW` shift-rotation over a large mixed constants table, `_0xNNNN`-style identifiers) and has no readable source, so its behavior cannot be inspected by Node-based tooling. The package advertises itself as a formatjs translation configuration helper; there is no functional need to fetch a second language runtime at preinstall to execute an opaque bundle. The Bun runtime download itself points at an official oven-sh release, but the code Bun then executes is the shipped obfuscated payload, not a build task. This is an alternate-runtime dropper: attacker-chosen bytes shipped in the tarball are executed on the installer's host at install time, evading Node-based static analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
